benefits: TQ4_1S shrinks the GGUF artifact to 4.16 GiB, 53.9% smaller than BF16 and 13.4% smaller than Q8_0.
It preserves the handoff path as a loadable GGUF with Turboquant metadata, useful for distribution and runtime integration experiments.
KV and recurrent-state allocations in this short run are not worse than BF16/Q8_0: 1024 MiB KV and 6432 MiB recurrent state.
costs: Current local llama.cpp/Turboquant path is not performance-ready: prompt throughput is 0.36% of BF16 and 0.32% of Q8_0; decode is 2.47% of BF16 and 1.70% of Q8_0.
Short held-out perplexity worsens to 1.91x BF16, while Q8_0 is 1.21x BF16.
Logits KL vs BF16 is higher than Q8_0: 1.8819 vs 1.64035 in the one-chunk logits probe.
The q8_0/q8_0 KV-cache bench was not common across all groups because BF16 failed context creation in that setting, so the paired analysis uses f16/f16 KV.
interpretation: Turboquant is currently best framed as a compact release/research handoff format, not the fastest serving path in this local build. Its main next milestone is runtime/kernel optimization and broader paired lm-eval validation.
